claim: The headline 'moderate to strong support for ACH, brainstorming, devil's advocacy' rests on one vote-count review (Coulthart) read only through its abstract and second-hand summaries; per-technique effect sizes are unchecked. Gap search: the abstract confirms a random sample of over 2,000 studies and a 21-student experiment; the per-technique counts are still unread (PDF behind a bot wall).
agent_test: Do not test; treat as a prior. Check by reading the 2017 IJIC paper.

claim: Only 6 of the 12 Primer SATs have any empirical test, and only 3 have more than low credibility.
agent_test: Rule, not test: no SAT enters the schema on authority.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: ACH as a whole gives little or no gain in judgment quality in human experiments with a no-SAT control (accuracy null in 3 of 3 studies that measured it; confirmation-bias cut in 1 of 4).
schema_part: hypothesis comparison operator (do not copy ACH scoring)
agent_test: Arms at equal tokens: plain, ACH-matrix prompt, code-scored Bayes matrix; score accuracy and Brier on items with known answers.

claim: ACH training improves cue-usefulness judgments in analysts, but not probability accuracy or coherence (N=50: MAE control .21 vs ACH .26, p=.14; usefulness r .68 vs .17).
agent_test: Compare LLM diagnosticity ratings with and without a separate evidence-rating call against true likelihood ratios. (a09 and b05 are the same trial.)

claim: Code-side post-processing (coherentizing, then averaging) beats the structured technique: 35% error cut from coherentizing, 61% from averaging 50 analysts; about 1 SD error cut in a lay panel.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare k independent samples averaged and normalised in code against one ACH-prompted answer.

claim: ACH-style matrix users double-count correlated cues and show pseudo-diagnosticity; ACH was less reliable than control (MAD .22 vs .18, d=.20, p=.051).
agent_test: Insert correlated evidence items; measure double counting with and without a matrix; handle dependence in code.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Humans often fail to follow ACH steps (38% compliance in law students; most ACH-trained analysts broke rules; 80% of controls built a matrix unprompted), so a protocol effect is hard to isolate.
agent_test: Compare instruction-only vs code-enforced step order on the same task.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Matrix layout matters: hypotheses in rows gave 39.2% choosing the confirming hypothesis vs 61.8% (columns) and 67.3% (text), N=161.
agent_test: Test row-wise vs column-wise hypothesis layout in the prompt at equal tokens.

claim: Confirmation bias is rarer than the ACH premise assumes: 66.1% of 62 Dutch military analysts were balanced; several studies found little bias to correct.
agent_test: Measure how often our agent anchors before adding any debiasing step; apply only on that signal.

claim: Process-quality scores follow technique count (r=.46 with QoR) but accuracy does not clearly (r=.23, p=.15); QoR to accuracy is weak (r=.25-.30).
agent_test: Never score the scaffold on process-looking output; score outcome accuracy. (Same Martin preprint in all lines.)

claim: Tradecraft-standard scoring is unreliable for one rater (ICC .366) and needs groups (3 raters .608).
agent_test: Use outcome labels or several judges, not one LLM judge, to grade reasoning quality.

claim: Task conflict does not reliably improve team outcomes: the 2003 meta-analysis found negative effects; the 2012 update (116 studies, 8,880 groups) did not replicate the strong negative effect and found benefits only under moderators.
agent_test: Abstract-only. Test dissent only under signals; see debate claims.

claim: Assigned dissent helps human decisions over consensus (Schwenk 1990). Recalled from memory, not verified.
agent_test: Verify source before use.

claim: Interacting brainstorming groups produce fewer ideas than nominal groups (Mullen 1991). Recalled, not verified; consistent with Coulthart's creativity finding.
agent_test: Compare k independent hypothesis lists merged in code with one shared-context list at equal tokens; count distinct valid hypotheses.

claim: Multi-agent debate beat single answer and self-reflection in the original LLM study (arithmetic 81.8 vs 67.0, MMLU 71.1 vs 63.9) with one model family.
agent_test: One team; later work does not confirm the lead at equal compute (next claim).

claim: Debate does not reliably beat self-consistency, Medprompt or a strong single prompt at equal compute (GSM8K, 6 responses: debate 83.2 vs self-consistency 85.3; 36-configuration study: MAD seldom beats CoT). Update: one 2026 equal-compute study (MMLU-Pro) puts debate 1.3 points above self-consistency, so the sign depends on setup; independent-first majority beat debate in Wynn 2025.
agent_test: Equal-token arms: debate vs self-consistency vs single prompt on our benchmark mix.

claim: Dissent strength has a task-dependent optimum: counterintuitive items gain (MAD 37.0 vs 26.0), routine items prefer agreement; strong forced disagreement was weakest in one study.
agent_test: Make dissent a signal-triggered dial; test on counterintuitive vs routine items.

claim: LLM agents conform: debate flips correct answers to wrong, most when alone in their answer; assistants give in under challenge.
agent_test: Give the critic no proposed answer; measure correct-to-wrong flip rate at equal tokens.

claim: Self-correction without an external signal lowers accuracy (GPT-3.5 CommonsenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0); oracle feedback rescues it.
agent_test: Revise only from real tool output; compare to blind self-critique on the current model (the tested models are old).

claim: A fixed ACH-style prompt gives a small zero-shot gain over an unstructured judge (about 2 points); a rigid scaffold alone can hurt (MMLU-Pro 49.4 vs 52.5 vanilla); big gains needed training. Update: on MuSR (10 models) a four-step structured pipeline beat direct by 13.2 points, but the ACH step added only 0.8 of that.
agent_test: Matrix step as an option triggered by a tie between candidates; compare to a plain judge.

claim: Composing 12 SAT skills into an LLM pipeline gave model-dependent results: arena rating from +88 to -60, no uniform gain; failure was candidate compression.
agent_test: Keep the wide candidate list to the end; test pipeline vs plain on our model.

claim: LLM hypothesis generation collapses onto a few modes as the valid space grows.
agent_test: Count unique valid hypotheses with and without stratified sampling.

claim: Role-diverse or model-diverse panels beat identical ones; same-role panels add little.
agent_test: Mix model families or personas vs same-prompt samples at equal tokens.

claim: A pre-action devil's-advocate check in an agent loop gave a small gain (WebArena 23.5 vs 22.7; plan revisions down 45%).
agent_test: Replicate on our tasks with confidence intervals.

claim: A small justified harness nearly matched a far larger one (83.8% at 3k lines vs 85.0% at 512k lines) on intelligence-analyst questions.
agent_test: Add scaffold parts only on an eval gain; drop unused ones.

claim: Code-checked ACH is feasible: base-rate weights and confidence caps set by code (cap 0.4 unless rarity >= 0.5); derived conclusions do not re-enter as evidence. Design only, not measured. Update: a related code-aggregated design (LEAP) was measured: FutureX .6512 to .7284 at matched tokens, dependency clustering worth 1.9 points.
agent_test: Test a code-weighted matrix vs an LLM-weighted matrix at equal tokens.

claim: Natural-frequency instruction improves analysts' Bayesian coherence; a Bayesian-network method beat unaided individuals by Glass delta 1.4-2.2.
agent_test: Prompt frequency-tree format vs probability format at equal tokens.

claim: No controlled LLM study tests pre-mortem, key assumptions check, red team or weighing-vs-seeking evidence on analyst-style tasks. Closest: a prompt-only pre-mortem for safety (harm score 3.22 to 2.19) and a position paper with no data.
agent_test: Our own tests would be new; see GAPS.

claim: A code-aggregated evidence step (model rates each item in isolation, code applies prior and Bayes update) beat a plain all-evidence judge at equal tokens on 5 current small and mid models (FutureX .6512 to .7284; ECE .184 to .088). Without the prior it fell below the plain judge.
agent_test: Run same design on investigation items with 4+ hypotheses and a prompt-only ACH arm at equal tokens.

claim: Collapsing same-source evidence by code before scoring reduces double counting: removing it cost 1.9 FutureX points and raised calibration error ECE from .088 to .158. LLMs themselves discount exact repeats but adopt verified-invalid candidates 93-100% of the time.
agent_test: Tag each item with a source key; dedupe in code; test paraphrased duplicates.

claim: Extra structure pays most on hard items, which can be detected by low agreement among independent samples: MMLU-Pro gain +2.2 (easy), +8.5 (medium), +9.0 (hard) at 15-20x compute; DynaDebate's diverse start matters on AIME (-6.7 points without it) but not MATH500 (-1.4).
schema_part: trigger for critic and matrix (S-state router)
agent_test: Trigger critic/matrix when k independent samples disagree or margin is low; log trigger rate and gain.

claim: In the one structured-investigation test on current models, the ACH matrix step added only +0.8 points over evidence filtering plus profiling (63.8 to 71.3 total with profiling); the gain came from filtering and profiling.
agent_test: Do not make ACH a default; keep filtering and per-suspect profiling; test ACH on 4+ hypothesis items.

claim: Telling a model to be correct does not stop conformity; flips to wrong answers rise when a correct agent is alone, and an argumentative thread raises sycophancy 2-3x (50% to 79% median). Blind first answers and code-made final choice are the structural fixes.
agent_test: Compare in-thread critic vs blind critic whose output code applies.

claim: Open: no direct LLM test found for hypothesis layout (rows vs columns) or for Schwenk 1990 / Mullen 1991 effect sizes; the nearest evidence is option-position bias (gold in slot D cost gpt-3.5 6.3 points).
agent_test: Permute hypothesis order across independent samples; test row vs column layout directly.
